---
title: "Classroom settings"
---

A class that signs in together puts a different load on JupyterHub than a handful of
researchers. Positron Server sessions are heavier than a plain kernel, and they all
start within the same few minutes. This page collects the JupyterHub settings that
matter most for that pattern, and explains what each one does.

Every setting on this page goes in `jupyterhub_config.py`, unless the text says
otherwise. Treat the values as starting points, then measure your own hardware and
class size and adjust.

## Settings at a glance

| Setting | JupyterHub default | Classroom starting point |
|---|---|---|
| `c.Spawner.default_url` | `''` (JupyterLab) | `/positron/?tkn=<token>` |
| `c.Spawner.start_timeout` | `60` | `120` |
| `c.Spawner.http_timeout` | `30` | `60` |
| `c.JupyterHub.concurrent_spawn_limit` | `100` | leave as is below 100 students |
| `c.JupyterHub.active_server_limit` | `0` (no limit) | the number of seats your memory supports |
| `c.Spawner.mem_limit` | `None` | `4G` |
| `c.Spawner.cpu_limit` | `None` | `1` |
| Idle culler timeout | `3600` in TLJH, no culler elsewhere | `3600` |

## Start students in Positron Server

A single-user server opens JupyterLab by default, and students reach Positron Server
from the launcher tile. `Spawner.default_url` changes where a session lands.

Positron Server validates a connection token on every request. The launcher tile
works because it carries that token as a `tkn` query parameter. A bare `/positron`
URL carries no token, so Positron Server answers `403 Forbidden`. To land students
in Positron Server, pin the token in the session environment and add it to the
landing URL:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
import os

POSITRON_TOKEN = "<paste your generated token here>"

c.Spawner.environment = {
    "PATH": "/opt/positron-server/bin:" + os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"),
    "POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN": POSITRON_TOKEN,
}

c.Spawner.default_url = f"/positron/?tkn={POSITRON_TOKEN}"
```

Generate the token once, then paste it into the config:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(16))"
```

A connection token accepts only the characters 0-9, a-z, A-Z, underscore, and
hyphen.

::: callout-note
On Positron Server 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2, add
`POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` to the same dictionary. See
[Verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd). Positron Server 2026.09.0 and newer
need no license variable, because `positron-server` validates its own license
file.
:::

::: callout-important
A pinned token is shared by every session, so it is no longer a per-session secret.
Keep `POSITRON_HOST` at its default of `127.0.0.1`. Positron Server then listens on
loopback inside each session, and the authenticated JupyterHub route remains the only
way in. Binding to `0.0.0.0` with a pinned token exposes the port to anyone who
learns the token.
:::

::: callout-note
Students still reach JupyterLab at `/user/<username>/lab` when they need the notebook
interface.
:::

## Give sessions time to start

Two Hub timeouts apply to a spawn. `start_timeout` bounds the spawn itself.
`http_timeout` bounds the wait for the single-user server to answer its first HTTP
request.

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
c.Spawner.start_timeout = 120
c.Spawner.http_timeout = 60
```

Raise these values when the single-user server is slow to come up. A loaded host, a
cold page cache at the start of a term, and a large image pull under DockerSpawner
all push past the defaults of 60 and 30 seconds.

::: callout-note
These timeouts do not govern Positron Server startup. `positron-server` starts on the
first request to `/positron`, which happens after the Hub considers the session
running. `jupyter-positron-server` waits up to 120 seconds for that startup,
independently of the Hub timeouts.
:::

## Handle a class signing in at once

`concurrent_spawn_limit` caps how many sessions start at the same time. Requests
above the cap receive a `429` response, and JupyterHub asks those students to retry
after 30 to 60 seconds. The default of 100 already covers a class of 40, so a lab of
that size needs no change.

Lower the limit only to protect a small host from a burst of heavy spawns:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
c.JupyterHub.concurrent_spawn_limit = 20
```

A lower number trades a slower sign-in rush for a calmer host. Students above the cap
wait and retry instead of landing on an overloaded machine.

`active_server_limit` caps how many sessions run at once, which is the setting that
protects total memory:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
c.JupyterHub.active_server_limit = 25
```

The default of `0` enforces no limit. To size this value, divide the memory available
for sessions by the per-session allocation. A host with 100 GB for sessions and 4 GB
per session supports 25 seats.

## Cap memory and CPU per session

A Positron Server session uses more memory than an RStudio session or a plain Jupyter
kernel. The [memory requirements](configuration.qmd#memory-requirements) section
recommends at least 2.5 GB per session, and 4 GB for a standard workload.

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
c.Spawner.mem_limit = '4G'
c.Spawner.cpu_limit = 1
```

::: callout-important
`mem_limit` is a hard cap, not a share. A session that reaches the cap is killed, so
a value below the recommended allocation produces crashes during memory-intensive
work. The 2 GB floor suits a light workload only.
:::

::: callout-note
JupyterHub does not enforce these limits itself. The spawner has to implement them.
SystemdSpawner (used by TLJH) and DockerSpawner both do. LocalProcessSpawner does
not, and passes the values to the session as environment variables only.
:::

On The Littlest JupyterHub (TLJH), set the same limits through `tljh-config`:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
sudo tljh-config set limits.memory 4G
sudo tljh-config set limits.cpu 1
sudo tljh-config reload
```

## Reclaim idle sessions

A student who closes a laptop leaves a session holding memory. The JupyterHub idle
culler stops sessions that report no activity for a set period.

TLJH runs the culler already, with a timeout of one hour and a check every ten
minutes. To change the timeout:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
sudo tljh-config set services.cull.timeout 7200
sudo tljh-config reload
```

On a Hub with no culler, such as the docker-compose template, install
`jupyterhub-idle-culler` into the same Python environment as the Hub, then register it
as a service:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
import sys

c.JupyterHub.services = [
    {
        "name": "idle-culler",
        "command": [
            sys.executable, "-m", "jupyterhub_idle_culler",
            "--timeout=3600",
            "--cull-every=300",
        ],
    },
    # On 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2, keep the positron-license service here too.
]

c.JupyterHub.load_roles = [
    {
        "name": "idle-culler-role",
        "services": ["idle-culler"],
        "scopes": [
            "list:users",
            "read:users:activity",
            "read:servers",
            "delete:servers",
        ],
    },
    # On 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2, keep the positron-license-service role here too.
]
```

::: callout-important
`c.JupyterHub.services` and `c.JupyterHub.load_roles` replace their lists rather than
adding to them. On Positron Server 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2, put the culler
entries in the same two lists that hold the `positron-license` entries from the
[verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd), or the license minting service stops
running.
:::

::: callout-note
Grant the culler its permissions through a role, as shown above. The older
`"admin": True` service field targets JupyterHub before version 2.0.
:::

::: callout-note
A browser tab left open on Positron Server counts as activity. Positron Server
exchanges a keepalive message with the browser every five seconds, and the proxy
records each one. The culler reclaims a session once the student closes the tab or
loses the connection, not while an idle tab stays open.
:::

## Lock Positron settings for a class

`POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` locks settings so students cannot change them. Two
settings come up often for coursework:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
# Add to the c.Spawner.environment dictionary defined above.
"POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS": '{"ai.enabled":false,"extensions.autoUpdate":false}',
```

- **`ai.enabled`**: set to `false` to turn off every Positron AI feature at once. To
  turn features off one at a time, see the
  [Positron AI configuration reference](https://positron.posit.co/ai-configuration.html).
- **`extensions.autoUpdate`**: set to `false` to hold extension versions steady across
  a class for the length of a term.

For version requirements and the full behavior of locked settings, see the
[admin-enforced settings](configuration.qmd#admin-enforced-settings) section.

::: callout-important
Each assignment to `c.Spawner.environment` replaces the whole dictionary. Set every
session variable in one assignment, including `PATH` from the
[Get started](get_started.qmd) guide.
:::
